# Northvale froze your money. It wasn't supposed to happen this way.

*By Inês — product designer at Pinha. Published Tuesday, 10 November 2026.*

Short version first, because you've been waiting four days and you deserve the facts before anything else: **your money is safe, it is not Northvale's money, and Northvale is not allowed to use it. But they are holding it, and I am not going to dress that up.**

Below is everything we know, in order, including the parts I hate most. I'll also tell you what we got wrong, because a lot of the anger you're feeling is pointed in the right direction, and some of it is pointed at us. Both are fair.

---

## What happened

On 4 November, Northvale Payments emailed us to say they were terminating our commercial agreement. Thirty days' notice, they wrote. No real reason attached — just a line about a "risk appetite review".

On Friday, 6 November, at 09:00, with no warning email, no call, nothing, they blocked **every outgoing transfer from Pinha**. Every withdrawal, to every one of you. They also stopped accepting incoming money, so your round-ups stopped too. That's why some of you are looking at a balance that hasn't moved since Thursday and is missing this month's round-up.

They had twenty-six days left on their own notice. They didn't use them.

Their account manager stopped answering our calls on Friday. His phone goes to a voicemail in Lithuanian. That's what the last four days have looked like from our side of the table.

I keep reading that email. "Risk appetite review." They wrote that the day before they froze 14,200 people's savings, and I'd like somebody at Northvale to explain to me what risk they were reviewing, because from where I'm sitting it looks less like prudence and more like them deciding early what to do with money that isn't theirs. They broke their own notice. That isn't risk management. That's cowardice, and it means every word of goodwill in that email was decorative.

## Where your money is right now

Let me be precise here, because this is the part that matters most and the part I refuse to let get buried under everything else.

Your balance is held by Northvale in a **safeguarded account**, separate from Northvale's own operating money. It is ring-fenced and it belongs to you. Northvale cannot spend it, lend it, invest it, or use it to cover their own losses. If their business fails, their money fails — yours does not go into the bankruptcy pile with it. That is what "safeguarded" means, and it is the whole reason the legal protection exists.

But I won't oversell it either. Safeguarded means **protected, not available on tap**. Northvale still holds the keys. Getting the balances out of them requires their cooperation, and moving them to our new partner requires a regulator's approval. So the honest sentence is this: *your money is yours and it is protected, and right now we cannot move a single euro of it until Northvale decides to let go and Banco de Portugal says we can.*

I wish I could tell you it's just a technicality. It isn't.

## What we're doing

- **A new partner, already signed.** Ostra Bank, in Lisbon. To move you over, we need two things: the balances file from Northvale, and Banco de Portugal's approval of the new arrangement.
- **How long.** Our honest estimate is **10 to 15 working days** for the migration once those two pieces are in place. I'm telling you that because it's what we believe today, not because I'm going to pin a date on your money. I can't tell you when Northvale will hand over the file. I can't tell you when the approval lands. Anyone who gives you a firm date right now is making it up, and you've had enough of other people's money being handled badly to know what that feels like.
- **Regulators.** On 7 November we filed a complaint with **Banco de Portugal** and with the **Bank of Lithuania**, the central bank that supervises Northvale. If you're in Spain and you want to file with the Banco de España as well, write to us and we'll send you the details.
- **Fees.** The monthly fee is cancelled for **November and December**, for everyone, whatever your plan. You will not pay us for a service you can't use.
- **Updates.** Every **Monday and Thursday** on this blog until this is over, even when the update is "nothing changed today". Especially then.

## What we got wrong

We had **one** payment partner. No second one, no fallback, no plan B sitting in a drawer. We called it simplicity. It was a single point of failure with fourteen thousand people's savings behind it, and we chose it.

I design the screens in this app. I designed the one that says **"your money is always yours, take it out anytime."** I look at it now and I feel physically ill, because Northvale made that sentence a lie on a Friday morning and I wrote it believing it was true. I wrote it because I believed we had built something where that was guaranteed. We hadn't built the guarantee. We had a promise and a hope.

You are allowed to be angry at us for that. I'm not going to tell you to calm down, and I'm not going to tell you this was "an industry situation" or "unforeseeable" or that we "take it very seriously". You took money out of your own pocket and trusted a small app in Lisbon to keep it safe. We were supposed to be the part of the system that didn't get to fail. We failed first, and then Northvale failed worse.

## What you can do now

**If your money is needed for something urgent — rent, a medical bill, you're losing your job, a deposit, a deadline:**
Write to **urgent@pinha.example** with the subject line **URGENTE**. Please include: your full name, the email or phone number registered on your account, the exact amount, what it's for, the date you need it by, and a document if you have one (a rental contract, an invoice, an unemployment record). We are pushing for individual releases from Northvale for these cases, one by one, and that is the only route that exists while the whole balance is frozen. The more concrete the request, the faster we can argue for it.

**If it's not urgent:** normal support channels, and **no, we know the reply time is around two days**. There are three of us answering email and 1,900 of you wrote in since Friday. I have no excuse for that number. If it's been more than two days and you haven't heard back, send it again — we won't mind, and we won't hold it against you.

**You don't need to do anything else.** Keep using Pinha normally. Don't delete the app, don't close your account, don't try to re-register. Your balance stays yours and it will follow you to the new partner when the migration happens. We will tell you before anything changes.

## The email from Porto

There's one I can't get out of my head.

A woman in Porto wrote to us, entirely in capitals, because she was angry and scared and typing fast. She has been saving for three years for a deposit on a car. The deadline she was given is **Friday, 13 November**.

I read that email on the metro and I nearly cried. I have read it more times since than I'd like to admit. Her deadline is three days after this post goes live, and I cannot stand here and tell you we will get her money out in time, because I don't know if Northvale will release it, and I don't know if Banco de Portugal can approve a release that fast. What I can tell you is that her email is at the top of the urgent queue, that we've written to Northvale about her specifically, and that if you are in her situation — *today* — write to urgent@pinha.example with subject URGENTE and say what the deadline is. Give us the date and we will use it.

Three years of round-ups toward a car, and a frozen account, and a Friday that arrives whether or not anyone's paperwork moves. I'm sorry. I'm sorry we were the ones holding that promise.

## Where this goes from here

Northvale has a complaint in front of two central banks, a signed replacement waiting, and a customer base that is now extremely public about how they were treated. There are legal routes available to us if the balances file doesn't arrive. I'll tell you about them when they become real, because until then they'd just be words.

What I know for certain is this: the money is safeguarded, it is legally yours, and every single one of you is going to get it back. Not as a favour. As a debt they owe.

We're going to be here on Monday and Thursday with updates. If something changes tomorrow, we'll say so tomorrow.

And if you want to be furious with Northvale — good. I am too. Just don't spend that anger on us. We've got enough to answer for.

**Inês**
Product designer, Pinha
Lisbon

reasons: Facts: the piece says the 'risk appetite' email came 'the day before' the freeze, but it was sent 4 Nov and the freeze was 6 Nov; it also says 'twenty-six days left' on the notice, when 6 Nov to 4 Dec is 28 days.
The post says the 4 November email came the day before the 6 November freeze, and its closing tells users not to direct anger at Pinha despite the requested acceptance of that anger.
